lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Check that the profile link is live and points to your actual profile, not a placeholder.
The birth date and nationality should not be on the résumé.
items.because: They aren’t needed to assess your qualifications and can expose you to irrelevant bias.

items.says: Make sure the MBA dates show accurately whether the degree is completed.
items.because: Its status should be accurate as of the version you send.

items.says: Consider spelling out the undergraduate degree.
items.because: That would avoid ambiguity around the abbreviation.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% conversion change is relative or a percentage-point improvement.
Give the measurement period or comparison basis for the conversion change.
Clarify the scope behind “all merchants.”
items.because: The claim could overstate the rollout.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution versus the team’s delivery.
items.because: The semicolon can blur ownership.

items.says: Make the feature’s scope and the two-week schedule result easier to understand.
State the currency of the chargeback-loss estimate.
Explain how six months of data supports an annual loss estimate.
Clarify whether the roadmap priority was adopted or the analysis informed a recommendation.
Change the British spelling “analysed” to match US conventions.
items.because: The rest of the résumé uses US conventions.

items.says: Explain what the 140 tickets represents.
items.because: It could mean resolved tickets, all tickets handled, or another measure.

items.says: Give the timing and comparison basis for the halved ticket queue.
items.because: A comparison period or starting count would make the reduction more credible.

items.says: Add a finding or remove the measurement-method bullet.
items.because: It only describes an approach and may add no useful evidence beyond the redesign result.

items.says: Acknowledge the limits of comparing merchants who opted in with those who did not.
items.because: The groups may differ for reasons unrelated to the redesign.

items.says: Make its relationship to the separate onboarding-redesign result clear.
items.because: The Harbor bullets overlap.

items.says: Clarify the pilot’s timing and denominator.
Make its relationship to the separate measurement bullet clear.
items.because: The Harbor bullets overlap.

items.says: The onboarding accomplishment is duplicated in the practicum section.
items.because: The same result should not appear as a separate accomplishment in multiple sections.

items.says: The late-delivery reduction comes from excluding weather-delayed shipments rather than improving deliveries.
items.because: Changing the calculation can look like metric manipulation without evidence of an operational improvement.

items.says: Add the measurement period for the pick-error reduction.
Clarify whether the 30% is a relative reduction or a percentage-point change.
“Prepares” has the wrong tense for a past role.
items.because: It does not match the other bullets.

items.says: Add the scale, decision, or outcome of the forecasting work, or omit the bullet.
items.because: It gives a responsibility but no result.

items.says: Clarify whether the annual driver hours saved were measured or estimated.
Clarify whether the savings were realized after rollout.
Clarify whether 3,100 students were reached, eligible, or actual users.
Explain the basis for the 9-tonne figure.

Specify the time period meant by “the following term.”
Clarify how the reminders’ contribution to usage growth was assessed.
Include the growth rate if available.
items.because: The bullet currently gives only starting and ending figures.

items.says: Give the total number of weekly pickup slots behind the 95% figure.
Identify the period over which the reduction in cover shifts was measured.
Say what the working sessions produced and how they affected scheduling decisions, or remove the bullet.
items.because: It describes an activity but not an outcome.

items.because: The current wording obscures who did it.

items.because: That would strengthen the adoption detail.
